headline: Tanker strikes cruise ship in New Orleans, sending passengers into river
author: Brady Dennis

paragraphs.text: The 7LIVEDeveloping stories we're following
National correspondent covering the Southeast

A tanker on Friday afternoon hit a passenger cruise ship that was docked along the Mississippi River in New Orleans, causing a massive emergency response that included firefighters rescuing people from the water.

Kimberly Curth, a Port of New Orleans spokeswoman, said the incident happened at approximately 12:30 p.m. local time when an Atlantic Asphalt tanker crashed into the docked American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage ship that had docked about two hours earlier.
An estimated 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, were aboard the American Heritage at the time, Curth said.

Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department, the U.S. Coast Guard and emergency medical personnel were on scene, conducting rescue and response operations.
Curth said passengers were being brought inside the port’s administration building “for triage and assistance.”

“Our immediate priority is the safety of all passengers, crew members and first responders,” she said in a statement. “This remains an active and evolving incident. The number of injuries and the cause of the collision have not yet been confirmed.”
Reporter covering politics with a focus on campaigns
Van Hollen ‘no longer pursuing’ possible 2028 bid as he seeks Senate leader job
Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) is abandoning his presidential ambitions for 2028 as he seeks instead to oust Sen. Chuck Schumer (D) from his leadership role.

“I’m no longer pursuing that,” Van Hollen said Friday of his potential 2028 presidential bid, after a speech to Democrats gathered in Denver to celebrate the party’s huge wins in the midterm elections and chart a cohesive path forward.

“I believe that the size and scale of these majorities provides an opportunity for the United States Senate to answer the call of the American people,” Van Hollen said. “We can’t go back to business as usual.”

He announced his challenge to Schumer, the Senate minority leader, late Thursday, sparking a public power struggle alongside the work to unite Democrats. Until this week, Van Hollen had been “kicking the tires” on a presidential bid.
Van Hollen, 67, said the election called for a generational shift and that Schumer, 75, represented a style of politics that voters wanted to change.

He again characterized himself as an underdog in his leadership competition with Schumer, who has led the chamber’s Democratic caucus since 2017. And he declined to publicly reveal how many fellow senators have agreed to support him. But Van Hollen said he spoke directly with Schumer about it.
“We understand that this will be a competition. I think it’s important to give Senate Democrats a choice. That’s what we just gave voters all over the country a choice. They chose change,” he said.
Reporter covering arts and culture
Stacey Abrams told Ava DuVernay to hold ‘14th’ until after midterms

Ava DuVernay’s first documentary in 10 years — titled “14th,” after the constitutional amendment that it traces — will arrive on Netflix on Dec. 4. That wasn’t always DuVernay’s plan: At one point, she wanted it to be released ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

“It was Stacey Abrams who said to me, ‘You shouldn’t do that,’” DuVernay said Thursday at the Global Women’s Summit hosted by The Washington Post. She added that Abrams, the former two-time candidate for Georgia governor and voting rights activist, thought the film “will be more needed and more instructive after” the elections.

Abrams is interviewed in “14th,” which follows the history of the amendment that grants birthright citizenship, protects due process and guarantees equal protection under the law. DuVernay felt compelled to make the documentary after the Trump administration tried to end birthright citizenship via executive order, setting off a wave of litigation before the Supreme Court affirmed in June that nearly everyone born on U.S. soil is a citizen.

“What she really was saying to me is that the opposition is not going away,” DuVernay told The Post’s Geoff Edgers, explaining why Abrams thought it made sense for “14th” to arrive after Nov. 3. “These ideas are not going away, the money behind it is not going away, and it will come back with a vengeance.”
Anchor of the Early Brief newsletter
Trump gives Scott Colom ‘a lot of credit’ for campaigning at a MAGA rally
President Donald Trump doesn’t often give Democrats much credit.
But in an interview Thursday, he praised Democrat Scott Colom, who defeated Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) in Mississippi in the midterms, for meeting with voters outside a Trump rally last month.

“I heard it the other day, where I had a rally there, and we had lines that went 10 miles long, and he campaigned on that line, telling everybody on the line what a good job he did,” Trump said during an interview on Stephen A. Smith’s “Straight Shooter” podcast. “I give him a lot of credit for that.”

Colom made reaching out to Trump supporters central to his campaign in Mississippi, reflecting how the state has consistently voted for Republicans and backed Trump by 22 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. Colom’s visit to the Trump rally gained widespread attention online.

“What are you expecting? I’ve never been to a Trump rally,” Colom asked people in line. “What matters to you as a veteran right now?” he asked one man, who told him about gun rights. Other voters told him they were worried about high gas prices and the Iran war.
“I walked the Trump rally line to listen, not make assumptions. I talked with voters, asked questions and heard what matters to them,” Colom wrote about his interactions.
Meteorologist covering significant weather events and climate trends
Why the polar vortex has forecasters on alert for Arctic cold in the U.S.
For weeks, the weather community has been buzzing about an unusual phenomenon unfolding one atmospheric layer above us in the stratosphere.
It’s called a sudden stratospheric warming and involves temperatures rising rapidly and winds weakening significantly some 20 miles above the North Pole.

These warming events are most common during winter, but they can sometimes can happen in late fall or early spring — and right now, the earliest one on record is occurring, among records dating to 1958.

This warming is destabilizing the polar vortex and has caused it to stretch beyond its typical length. The vortex normally keeps frigid air locked up near the pole, but this disturbance could unleash it southward into areas where more people live.

That would only happen if stratospheric patterns filter down to the troposphere, which is the atmospheric layer where weather takes shape. Meteorologists liken this atmospheric-filtering process to “dripping paint.”

Late last November, a stratospheric warming event quickly dripped from the stratosphere to the troposphere, influencing a cold and snowy stretch across the United States that lasted for a month or two.

This year, the influence of this polar vortex disruption is looking less concrete, though some meteorologists are increasingly flagging the potential for it to play some role in U.S. weather patterns from late November into December.
However, its effects could be muted by a record El Niño, which has fueled an exceptionally mild start to November across much of the country.

If the polar vortex unleashes even a brief surge of icy air into the U.S., it would probably increase the chances for a blockbuster winter storm or two before the end of the year — especially when combined with El Niño’s heightened levels of atmospheric moisture.
The next ‘Bachelor’ star is Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman
Sam Hartman, a 27-year-old quarterback on the Washington Commanders’ practice squad, will be the next star of ABC’s “The Bachelor.”
Hartman, who will be asked to date 20 to 30 women at once before choosing a fiancée, said Friday on “Good Morning America” that he’s “very nervous.”
“I have a tough time holding conversation with one girl,” he said. “30 is going to be pretty tough.”

Hartman set various school records while playing college football at Wake Forest. In 2022, he was diagnosed with Paget-Schroetter syndrome and received the ACC’s Brian Piccolo Award for courage. He transferred to Notre Dame for his final season in 2023.
Hartman signed with the Commanders as an undrafted free agent in 2024. He has not yet appeared in a regular season game, spending most of his time on the team’s practice squad.
Asked what he looks for in a partner, Hartman said he likes “competitiveness.” He continued, “They have a drive for something that motivates me to wake up every day and chase them.”

His casting came after ABC pulled Taylor Frankie Paul’s season of “The Bachelorette” three days before its debut in the wake of domestic abuse reports. Season 30 of “The Bachelor” will premiere March 21 on ABC.
Reporter covering food news and trends
3 recipes that show sweet potatoes are more than just a Thanksgiving side
Sweet potatoes aren’t just for holiday dinners.

Beyond a marshmallow crown, they seemingly can do it all, including main courses, salads and even desserts. And their flavor offers loads of options, too — the vitamin-packed tubers’ earthy sweetness works just as well with the heat of chili powder as it does with baking spices.
Celebrate the sweet potato every day with these recipes. And if those don’t hit the sweet (potato) spot, you’ll find more here and in The Washington Post’s vast recipe database.

Loaded Sweet Potatoes With Chili Black Beans (pictured above): Potatoes sub for tacos when topped with all kinds of Tex-Mex fillings, such as cilantro and pickled jalapeños. (You can get creative with whatever condiments and bits of vegetables you have in your fridge, and do a taco-bar-style serving setup.) This hearty dish is a meal in itself.

Sweet Potato Salad With Orange-Maple Dressing: This side dish can be a vibrant accompaniment to a holiday meal, but you don’t need to wait for a special occasion to break it out. The ingredients both lean into the potatoes’ sweetness (that’s a job for raisins and maple) and serve as a foil for it (think zesty orange and verdant parsley).

Sweet Potato Spice Cake: Molasses and baking spices are classic companions in this Bundt cake, which is so beloved by readers that it made our hall-of-fame lineup. You can swap in a can of pumpkin puree if you have one left over from holiday pies.
